body:
### Description The following code: Running "php-cgi -i" on mips device Resulted in this output: ``` TERM vt100 SHELL /bin/bash OLDPWD / USER admin PROMPTLENGTH 11 ALU_SESMGR_RSP_SESS_IDX 0 ALIASES sh="show" ALU_SESMGR_RSP_AUTH_RD0 0x00000000 PATH /flash:/bin:/sbin:/usr/bin:/usr/sbin ALU_SESMGR_RSP_AUTH_RD1 0x00000000 ALU_SESMGR_RSP_AUTH_RD2 0x00000000 ALU_SESMGR_RSP_AUTH_RD3 0x00000000 PWD /flash PS1 TAURUS #-> HISTIGNORE &:*password* PS2 (Continue command from previous line or Ctrl/C) -> HOME /flash SHLVL 2 ALU_SESMGR_RSP_AAA_OPTS 0 LOGNAME admin PROMPT_COMMAND stty echo icrnl && setPrompt _ ./php-cgi

Fri Jun 14 02:47:57 : COREDUMPER ALRM message: Segmentation fault (core dumped) ``` _emalloc_48 will cause the panic , and is there any solution for it? But I expected this output instead: ``` Normal running ``` ### PHP Version PHP 8.3.4 ### Operating System linux 4.4 and arch is mips

comments.author: participant1
comments.body:
You might be able to use objcopy to separate debug symbols from the binary as follow :

```
objcopy --only-keep-debug sapi/cgi/php-cgi sapi/cgi/php-cgi.dbg
objcopy --strip-debug sapi/cgi/php-cgi
objcopy --add-gnu-debuglink=sapi/cgi/php-cgi.dbg sapi/cgi/php-cgi
```

then this sapi/cgi/php-cgi.dbg needs to be transferred as well into your device.
you can then launch gdb like this

```
gdb --args sapi/cgi/php-cgi -i
> symbol-file sapi/cgi/php-cgi.dbg
> r
...
```

Hope it helps and works :)

After that, won t be able to help for few hours unless someone chimes in ;)
